query: For refractory materials, experiments at the solid-to-fluid transition are difficult and yield sparse, scattered data, while the large compositional space of high-entropy systems makes systematic screening impractical. DFT free-energy studies can determine the transition from the crossing of solid and dense-fluid Gibbs energies and provide associated thermodynamic properties, but their reliance on extensive ab initio molecular dynamics makes them costly. TOR-TILD has shown high efficiency for elemental and binary systems, yet becomes substantially slower for multicomponent systems. Any broadly useful approach must retain ab initio-level accuracy, represent all thermodynamic effects identified as important, treat both phases around the transition, and remain practical across relevant compositions and temperatures. For a multicomponent high-entropy material in these high-temperature states, what single intervention could improve determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and causal mechanism, its predicted outcome relative to existing experimental and computational baselines, its boundary conditions, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive experiment or benchmark that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The incorporation of machine learning algorithms in the CALPHAD approach can improve the determination of transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity in multicomponent high-entropy materials.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy material in a solid state
generation.intervention: Incorporation of machine learning algorithms in the CALPHAD approach
generation.structural_mediator: Configurational entropy, short-range ordering/clustering (SRO/SRC), nanostructure phase-instabilities and nanostructure morphologies
generation.mechanism: The machine learning algorithms can efficiently screen and analyze the vast compositional space of high-entropy materials, identifying the optimal compositions and processing conditions that lead to improved thermodynamic properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved accuracy and efficiency in determining transition temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, volume change, and dense-fluid heat capacity
generation.baseline: Traditional CALPHAD approach without machine learning algorithms
generation.boundary: Limited to high-entropy materials with multiple principal elements, high-temperature states, and solid-to-fluid transition
generation.uncertainty: The accuracy of the machine learning algorithms depends on the quality and size of the training dataset, and the complexity of the high-entropy material systems

falsification_experiment.design: Comparison of the CALPHAD approach with and without machine learning algorithms in determining thermodynamic properties of high-entropy materials
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the incorporation of machine learning algorithms does not improve the accuracy and efficiency of determining thermodynamic properties, the hypothesis is falsified.

The chemical space of the investigated materials increases as more elements are added or exchanged. Additionally, by varying even one experimental parameter (e.g., an extra heat treatment during sample fabrication) will require an extra characterization for each of the produced samples, leading to more data points to be collected and interpreted. A concept for accelerated assessment of MPEAs has recently been proposed. Here we develop and apply this idea to quickly identify, screen and analyze structural alloys for use at moderate and high temperatures. We select a palette of 26 metallic elements that are most likely to produce the moderate and high-temperature properties ranges in MPEAs. The palette of elements is shown in Supplementary Table 1. Phase diagrams are the road maps for materials design, and give essential information on the phases present at a given alloy chemistry and temperature. Most binary and some ternary phase diagrams have been determined experimentally, but multi-component systems remain largely unexplored. Experimental measurement of multi-component phase diagrams is impractical due to the tremendous amount of work involved. In recent years, integration of the CALPHAD approach with key experiments has been demonstrated as an effective approach to determine complicated multi-component phase diagrams. The essence of the CALPHAD approach is to use experimental data from constituent binary and ternary phase diagrams to develop a thermodynamic database. High entropy alloys (HEAs), which contain multiple principal elements, have recently attracted considerable research interest due to their exceptional mechanical and physical properties, such as high corrosion, wear, fatigue resistances, yield strength, ductility, and thermal stability,, often outperforming traditional alloys and super-alloys, especially at low and high temperatures,. However, the design (compositional and chemical) space of HEAs is vast, which makes the use of the conventional methods based on lengthy, costly, high-fidelity (HF) approaches, a daunting task. An efficient strategy is thus highly demanded to screen and design HEAs with optimal mechanical and physical properties for specific applications,. Machine learning (ML) is emerging as a powerful tool for inductive screening and phase selection of HEAs. However, the accuracy of ML is strongly dependent on the size and quality of used dataset . The lack of a large-size, high-quality dataset for HEAs is currently a major challenge for using ML.
